name: Risdiplam
route_note: Once-daily oral solution (or via feeding tube); a film-coated tablet was approved in 2025.
targets: SMN2 pre-mRNA (exon 7 5' splice site and exonic splicing enhancer 2)
originator: PTC Therapeutics and the SMA Foundation, developed with Roche

discovery.by: PTC Therapeutics, SMA Foundation and Roche
discovery.note: Identified from a high-throughput screen for small molecules that promote SMN2 exon 7 inclusion, then optimised for selectivity. Year the compound was first described in the literature (Ratni et al., J. Med. Chem. 2018).

tagline: First oral treatment for spinal muscular atrophy
summary: Risdiplam is an orally available small molecule that corrects SMN2 splicing to raise SMN protein throughout the body. Approved in 2020, it was the first at-home oral treatment for spinal muscular atrophy.
mechanism: Risdiplam binds two sites on SMN2 pre-mRNA — the 5' splice site of intron 7 and exonic splicing enhancer 2 in exon 7 — stabilising the interaction with the U1 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein and promoting inclusion of exon 7.
Because it distributes systemically, it increases functional SMN protein in both the central nervous system and peripheral tissues.
uses: Spinal muscular atrophy in patients of all ages

history.title: Splicing modifiers described
history.detail: Naryshkin et al. (Science) report orally available SMN2 splicing modifiers from the PTC/Roche/SMA Foundation programme.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: In August the FDA approves Evrysdi for SMA in patients aged 2 months and older, based on FIREFISH and SUNFISH.

history.title: Newborns
history.detail: The FDA extends approval to infants under 2 months based on the RAINBOWFISH study.

history.title: Tablet formulation
history.detail: The FDA approves a 5 mg tablet that can be swallowed whole or dispersed in water.

pk.bioavailability: not determined in humans; well absorbed orally
pk.metabolism: mainly FMO1 and FMO3, also CYP3A

serious: Possible impairment of male fertility (animal data)

facts: Risdiplam is one of the first approved small molecules that work by targeting RNA splicing.

references.title: Ratni H et al. Discovery of risdiplam (J Med Chem 2018)
